title: Advising students to join the Navy
summary: Too many schools turn out too many musicians.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: It got too complicated for me. So as far as a future in musicianship, with all these schools turning people around -- I don't know if I told this or not in one of the earlier times, but in case I did I'll make it fairly short.

With the National Jazz Ensemble, I was asked to give a little talk, we used to do these so-called symposiums. It was the wrong term, it was lectures, not a symposium. And one thing they wanted to know, what do you advise us to do? I said, I advise you to join the Navy and learn a good trade.

There's 50, 100 schools, turning out 200 musicians a year. There aren't that many musicians working, you know. And it's very misleading. These schools are putting in their programs and showing these kids, telling them, you know, you're going to get work. They're not going to get work. And being a musician now isn't like you could be a shipping clerk and
you decide you want to go play trumpet someplace and you go out and get a job on trumpet.
